verses.english: Desire for rebirth in the realm of luminous form, desire for rebirth in the formless realm, conceit, restlessness, and ignorance.
These are the five higher fetters.

verses.pali: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ uddhambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya cattāro sammappadhānā bhāvetabbā.
verses.english: The four right efforts should be developed for the direct knowledge, complete understanding, finishing, and giving up of these five higher fetters.
It’s when a mendicant generates enthusiasm, tries, makes an effort, exerts the mind, and strives so that bad, unskillful qualities don’t arise. …

verses.pali: uppannānaṁ kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṁ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṁ ārabhati cittaṁ paggaṇhāti padahati.
verses.english: so that skillful qualities that have arisen remain, are not lost, but increase, mature, and are completed by development.

verses.pali: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ uddhambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya ime cattāro sammappadhānā bhāvetabbā”ti.
verses.english: These four right efforts should be developed for the direct knowledge, complete understanding, finishing, and giving up of these five higher fetters.”
(Tell in full as in SN 45.171–179, with the above as the final discourse.)
aggregates, and fetters high and low.
The Linked Discourses on the Right Efforts is the fifth section.
